newsitem.title: USA: Clear weather seen for U.S. HRW wheat harvest.
newsitem.headline: Clear weather seen for U.S. HRW wheat harvest.

text.p: Hot weather from Kansas to Texas Tuesday dried wheat fields and with forecasts for mostly clear weather through the weekend, meteorologists said harvesting should continue the next several days, meteorologists said.
Some scattered showers were likely Friday and Saturday from southern Kansas to Texas, but should not interrupt harvest in many areas.
"They probably will not be enough to be a major concern to the harvest," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
Temperatures soared to 100 to 105 degrees F in some areas of western Kansas Tuesday, which dried fields, said Burgio.
Cool weather will spread from Kansas to Texas Wednesday to Friday, producing scattered showers in less than half the area.
"I don't foresee any major harvest delays for the next week to 10 days," said Solberg of the hard red winter wheat area.
